items.title: Multi-frustum stencil clear is implicit / default-driven (NEEDS-VERIFICATION)
items.claim: The inter-frustum re-open sets depthLoadOp but never stencilLoadOp; stencil may not clear between frustums.
items.evidence: WebGPURenderTarget.getDepthStencilAttachment defaults stencilLoadOp to 'clear' and emits it whenever the format carries stencil (WebGPURenderTarget.ts:398-424); the inter-frustum depth-clear re-open at WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:2186-2207 calls it with defaults, so depth AND stencil clear between frustums, matching WebGL. Verified by code read (no batch).

items.title: Shadow cast path uses raw color command instead of a dedicated cast pipeline (NEEDS-VERIFICATION)
items.claim: Cast may use the colour pipeline; alpha-tested casters may cast opaque cards.
items.evidence: Dedicated depth-only cast pipelines exist: SHADOW_CAST_VARIANTS registry keyed by vertex layout (WebGPUShadowMapRenderer.js:652-720, _inferShadowLayoutKey), per-shadow-map castPipelines map :797-897, depth-only target :3/:104-113, CSM cast in WebGPUCSMCastPass.ts:454; terrain casters via prepareTerrainShadowCastCommandUniforms. ISSUES_AND_FIXED_BUGS.md:214 chains B-1/B-2 <-> C-R10/H-R2/H-R12 as fixed. Residual: the cast WGSL (Shaders/WebGPU/Shadow/ShadowMap.wgsl) contains no alpha / discard path and WebGPUShadowMapRenderer.js has no alpha-mode handling (rg -i alpha = 0 hits), so MASK/BLEND materials still cast their full silhouette; only a stochastic-dither chunk is noted as 'available for translucent shadow casts' (DEFERRED_WORK.md:7941), no row.
items.migrate_text: The WebGPU shadow-cast path is a dedicated depth-only pipeline family (WebGPUShadowMapRenderer.js:652-897 SHADOW_CAST_VARIANTS / castPipelines; WebGPUCSMCastPass.ts:454), so the original 'raw colour pipeline' premise is closed. What remains is alpha-test parity: Shaders/WebGPU/Shadow/ShadowMap.wgsl has no alpha-mask discard and the renderer never inspects the caster's alphaMode, so a MASK-textured leaf or fence casts its full quad on WebGPU where WebGL's cast derived command keeps the alpha test. This needs a cast variant that samples baseColor+alphaCutoff (or the csm_stochasticDither chunk noted at DEFERRED_WORK.md:7941) plus a probe over a masked-foliage glTF; no row tracks it today.

Severity is now low because the live WGSL path is WebGPUShaderModuleCache (keyed sourceId+defines, Batches 22-27) and the pipeline key folds module identity (Batch 825); WebGPUShaderCache is only reached through context.shaderCache (WebGPUContext.ts:4242) and WebGPUBufferPrimitiveRenderer.ts:600 explicitly declines to use it. items.migrate_text: WebGPUShaderCache.ts:414-418 still keys compiled modules on descriptor.name alone and :430 returns a constant false from isDestroyed(); two callers that register different WGSL under one name would share the first module. The defect is latent rather than live: every Cesium-authored WGSL renderer now goes through WebGPUShaderModuleCache.getOrCreate (sourceId + defines key) and WebGPURenderPipelineCache folds module identity into its key, so the name-keyed cache is a legacy side path reached only via context.shaderCache (WebGPUContext.ts:4242). Disposition should be either to hash the source into the key or to retire the class during the DX decomposition wave; either way it needs a spec with a runner home.

items.evidence: Globe receive: WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:896-912 resolves the receive shadow map per tile provider (plus point-light receive Batch 108, GlobeTerrain.wgsl:650-720); globe cast: WebGPUShadowMapRenderer.js:50 treats Pass.GLOBE commands as casters with prepareTerrainShadowCastCommandUniforms (:19), CSM cast WebGPUCSMCastPass.ts:38, exaggeration-aware cast noted DEFERRED_WORK.md:9863; clipping polygons on the WebGPU path GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js:696-703 / WebGPUVectorTileResources.ts. Globe pickId is not a WebGL feature either (globe picking is depth-based on both backends).
items.migrate_text: Definition only: resolved (globe casts and receives, clipping polygons wired).

items.title: getPooledBuffer is unkeyed on usage flags
items.claim: Pool keyed on string type only; a VERTEX|COPY_DST request can receive a VERTEX|STORAGE buffer.
items.evidence: WebGPUContext.ts:5705-5735 still keys _bufferPool on `type` and matches on size only (:5714-5716), ignoring `usage`. Mitigating fact: no engine code calls context.getPooledBuffer (rg '.getPooledBuffer(' over packages/engine/Source finds only the definition and an unrelated WebGPUResourceManager.ts:181 method), so the defect is unreachable today. No row.
items.migrate_text: WebGPUContext.getPooledBuffer (WebGPUContext.ts:5705-5735) still keys its pool on the string `type` and a size band, never on the requested `usage`, so the first caller that asks for a different usage under the same type can be handed a buffer whose usage bits do not match and fail at bind-group creation. The API currently has zero callers in packages/engine/Source, which is why it has never fired; it should be keyed on (type, usage) or deleted as dead surface when WebGPUContext.ts is decomposed in the DX wave.

items.title: _destroyFeatureRenderers partially no-ops for critical FRs
items.claim: ~13 FRs (PRIMITIVE, GLOBE_SURFACE, ...) lack destroy callbacks; WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.destroy() is never invoked; per-tile caches leak.
items.evidence: GraphicsContext._destroyFeatureRenderers (GraphicsContext.ts:2340-2357) no longer invokes destroy callbacks at all — it invalidates pending loaders and nulls the registry because device teardown releases GPU resources; scene-side destroy runs from scene objects (e.g. destroyWebGPUModelResources). Most listed keys now carry destroy callbacks anyway (PRIMITIVE, SUN, SKY_ATMOSPHERE, CUBE_MAP_PANORAMA, GAUSSIAN_SPLAT, POINT_CLOUD, POINT_CLOUD_EDL, VOXEL_PRIMITIVE in WebGPUFeatureRenderers.ts:380-740). The globe surface renderer is a per-device WeakMap singleton (GlobeSurfaceTileProviderRendering.js:1110-1160) whose lifetime is the GPUDevice's; its destroy() (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:2956) has no caller, but the device WeakMap collects it with the device.
items.migrate_text: Premise gone: the destroy-callback registry is no longer the teardown mechanism.

items.title: ClearCommand colorMask for channel-selective clear
items.claim: WebGPU clearValue has no per-channel mask; a ClearCommand with renderState.colorMask clears all four channels.
items.evidence: WebGPUContext.clear() (WebGPUContext.ts:4414-4589) consumes CesiumClearCommand {color, depth, stencil, framebuffer} (:318-327); no colorMask field or masked-clear pipeline exists (rg colorMask in WebGPUContext.ts = 0 hits). No row; no known upstream ClearCommand relies on a channel mask, so severity is low/latent.
items.migrate_text: WebGPUContext.clear() (WebGPUContext.ts:4414-4589) still models a ClearCommand as {color, depth, stencil, framebuffer} (:318-327) and ignores renderState.colorMask, so any WebGL ClearCommand that clears a subset of channels clears all four on WebGPU. No shipped Cesium path is known to depend on a masked clear, which is why it has never surfaced; the honest fix is a full-screen write-masked clear pipeline behind the ClearCommand path, and the finding should stay listed as a latent parity gap until a consumer appears.

items.title: Depth clip (depth-clip-control) never enabled
items.claim: unclippedDepth is forwarded but never set; depth-clip-control not in requiredFeatures.
items.evidence: WebGPURenderPipelineCache.ts:826 forwards descriptor.primitive?.unclippedDepth and :1072 keys on it, but no producer sets it; requiredFeatures come only from user options (WebGPUContext.ts:384, :1318) and 'depth-clip-control' appears nowhere in Renderer/WebGPU. No row. Log depth (frag_depth) handles Cesium's far-plane math on WebGPU, which is why this has not bitten.
items.migrate_text: WebGPU still always clips depth: WebGPURenderPipelineCache.ts:826/:1072 forward and key primitive.unclippedDepth, but nothing sets it and 'depth-clip-control' is never requested (requiredFeatures is user-supplied only, WebGPUContext.ts:1318). Because the fork's WebGPU path writes logarithmic depth through frag_depth, the globe far-plane case the 2026-04-16 review worried about does not manifest; the item is a latent parity difference for any command that relied on GL's default depth clamping and should remain a documented non-goal until a probe shows a difference.
